title: Syllabus
text:
Course Objectives
This course leads the students to understand the need of programming in various disciplines, basic concepts of algorithm, the process of computational problem solving in an efficient manner, how to write simple programs using C, pointers, dynamic memory allocation, arrays, functions, recursions, file handling and error handling, and basic concepts of modularity.

title: Syllabus
text:
Course Outcomes
At the end of the course students will be able to:

Implement a given algorithm in C by using standard programming constructs such as pointers, arrays, repetitions, functions, modules, aggregated data (arrays, lists, etc.).
Explain the output of a given C program, and identify and correct errors in a given C program (debug).
Write simple programs to solve math problems using the C programming language.

title: Syllabus
text:
Course Contents
Basic information about the computer; number systems and arithmetic; C program structure; programming types; compiler, interpreter; syntax of the C programming language; data types; operators and operator precedence; conditional statements; iterative statements (for, while, do-while); pointers; dynamic memory allocation; arrays; functions; string processing; file handling; error handling; header files; structures and unions in C.

Detailed Lecture Contents (28 hours)

Hours




Introduction: Introduction to Computer Science; Computer Algorithms; Computer Hardware; Computer Software

Number systems, conversions, and arithmetic
4


Programming types (declarative, imperative); C program structure (source files, assembly files, object files, linker, loader); compiler, interpreter
4


Data and expressions: literals, variables and identifiers, operators, expressions and data types; control structures: boolean expressions, selection control, iterative control
5


Pointers (pointer variables); arrays; dynamic memory allocation (malloc, calloc, realloc); functions and recursive functions
8


Function pointers; structure, union; file handling; error handling

text:

Acknowledgement



We are deeply grateful to Prof. Shweta Agrawal and the Department of Computer Science & Engineering, IIT Madras, for generously permitting the reuse and modification of this material. The original course page is here.
